title: RAW_UNSCREENED: Operations- und Ergebnisrahmen als Registertrennprobe
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: Wellcome MS 542 separates named qualities/states from explicit operations and named outputs; this gives a concrete gate for reading the bound HERB4 lines as descriptive records or executable processes.

design.scope_description: Nur die bereits gebundenen vollständigen HERB4-Linien f17r.5, f21r.12, f29v.1 und f29v.4 sowie die quellengebundenen W542/W541-Vergleiche in GDT625/GDT768; keine neue Seite, kein Bildzugriff und keine Bedeutungsfestlegung.
design.mechanism: A descriptive register stores material/part and quality/degree fields without temporal entailment; an executable recipe register requires a separate written operation frame between an input and a reached state, and a written result or closure when one is claimed.
design.unit: Exact complete-line surfaces and their recurring whole-form positions, preserving the bound line boundaries and all three manuscript readings.
design.contrast: Glossary/list record versus ordered recipe process with explicit operation and result obligations.
design.prediction: The glossary reading predicts that adjacent nominal-looking fields can co-occur without an operation/result pair and that their order is record-field order. The recipe reading predicts a reusable operator-position whole between input and state, plus a distinct output/closure position; a state-like neighbor alone cannot count as the operation.
concrete_observations: GDT768 records the exact f17r.5 surface `ychekchy cthy chor shor cphor cphaldy dair cthey qody`, including the adjacent triple `cthy chor shor` and later `dair cthey qody`.

GDT625 records the exact f29v.1 surface prefix `kooiin shor chetchy ol ls shytchy cthy shy cho shy daiin` and f29v.4 `ysho otshy okaiin cthy oltchy s shot sho okaiin`; their current state/part labels remain exploratory.

The bound primary comparator W542 fol.79v writes `ponatur super carbones` and separately `ponatur calidum super caput`; fol.80r writes `bene ablutae et pistatae`, `ponantur in vino albo`, `deinde distillentur`, `fiat aqua`; fol.118r-119v places learned part/drug names beside quality and degree fields.
linked_consequences: If HERB4 is a glossary/list, the f17r.5 nominal run should be admissible without inventing an unmarked action, and repeated quality/state forms should remain field descriptions across comparable lines.

If HERB4 is procedural, at least two complete lines must expose the same operator-slot whole between an input-like field and a state/result endpoint, while a distinct closure/output slot recurs; otherwise the process reading has no written bridge.

W542 predicts that a candidate state form and a candidate operation form must occupy different reusable positions, and that a claimed product/result must have an independent closing form rather than being inferred from a quality adjective.
design.nearest_rival: A uniform record grammar in which apparent operators and results are omitted or folded into whole-phrase semantics, allowing either reading to relabel the same sequence without a reusable frame.
design.distinguishing_observation: On the already bound complete lines, freeze recurring whole-form positions before glossing and ask whether one exact operator candidate recurs in the input-to-state slot and one independent closure candidate recurs after it across at least two lines. A line that only contains adjacent part/quality/value candidates distinguishes neither mechanism; it must remain unresolved.
assumption_costs: The W542 register distinction transfers as a structural expectation to HERB4.
Complete-line boundaries and recurrence positions inherited from GDT625/GDT768 are reliable under ZL3b/IT2a/RF1b.
The proposed operator and closure classes can be tested without assigning English meanings to any Voynich form.
design.strongest_likely_failure: The exposed HERB4 lines may contain no independent operation/result frame, so a process account and a field-list account remain observationally equivalent; GDT625 already warns that f29v.4 is more economically a pair of part-state descriptions than one drying process.

primary_sources.source_consequence: The reached state `calidum` is written with a separate placement/heating phrase, not used as the operation itself.
Operations are ordered by independent verbs and `deinde`, and the output is named by `fiat aqua`.
Named drug/part entries are paired with quality and degree in a descriptive glossary register.
